footer.tagline: A physical status light for your coding agent.

home.title: Know your agent's state without staring at a terminal.
home.subtitle: A physical desktop status light for Claude Code and CLI coding agents — green, yellow, red, at a glance.
home.stripAriaLabel: Simulated status light cycling through idle, working, waiting, and compacting states

whatItIs.heading: A status light you don't have to look for.
whatItIs.body: Ten addressable LEDs behind a diffuser, wired to a USB-C dev board, driven by a small Python CLI. Claude Code hooks flip its color automatically — green while the agent's working, yellow when it's waiting on you, red when it's idle. No dashboard, no extra window.

whyItExists.heading: Built for the tab you keep checking.
whyItExists.body: Coding agents run in the background, but "in the background" still means glancing at a terminal window every few minutes to check if it's stuck waiting on you. This moves that one bit of information off the screen entirely — walk away, glance at the light, know exactly where things stand.

waiting.label: Waiting
waiting.description: It needs you — a permission or an answer.

openHardware.heading: Open hardware, honestly a hobby project.
openHardware.body: MIT-licensed — schematics, firmware, and CLI all included. Five units built and tested, Linux and Windows supported today. Not a commercial product, not for sale. Built because a physical light is more fun to build, and more useful to have, than another terminal tab.

closing.heading: See it, build it, or just read about it.
